steps.text: Acids and bases have opposite properties. Let's identify substances by tapping them in the game below.
Tap “Lemon” — an acid. Notice it's sour and turns blue litmus red.
Now tap “Soap” — a base. It feels slippery and turns red litmus blue.
Tap “Water” — it's neutral, so litmus doesn't change at all.
Compare the results: acids are sour and turn litmus red; bases feel soapy and turn litmus blue. Never taste substances to test them — always use an indicator!

coach.mission: Identify each substance as acid, base, or neutral.
whenStuck: Tap a substance to test its properties.
Acids are sour and turn litmus red; bases feel soapy and turn it blue.
whenWrong: Sour + turns blue litmus red = acid; slippery + turns red litmus blue = base. Re-check the clue.
Water is neutral — litmus doesn't change for it.
whenCorrect: Right — you matched the property to the substance!
coach.done: You've compared the properties of acids and bases. Explore more, or move on.
